title: DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 -> 128 (grad_accum 2 -> 1)
description: One constant: DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 -> 128, so the 2^18-token optimizer step is one fwd/bwd instead of two accumulated micro-steps; identical math, nothing else changed.
reflection: val_bpb 0.985624 vs the 0.987227 baseline (-0.0016), but the mechanism I bet on did NOT show up and I do not think the win is real. Throughput barely moved: 1135 steps / 297.5M tokens / MFU 42.56% against the baseline's 1121 / 293.9M / 42.03% - only +1.2% tokens, not the 3-8% I predicted before the run. By the cell's own token/loss calibration (~0.03-0.04 bpb per doubling of tokens) 1.2% is worth about -0.0006, so at most a third of the delta is explained by the change; the rest is a ~2 sigma draw on a flat surface (round-3 arm-to-arm sd 8e-4). Averaged final train loss agrees with that reading: mean of the last 60 logged values is 2.7646 vs the baseline's 2.7625, i.e. very slightly WORSE on training data despite seeing 1.2% more of it, while val came out better. Two hard facts worth keeping regardless: (1) the gradient-accumulation boundary at 2^18/depth-10 costs ~1% of throughput, not more - the per-step overhead this cell has been blaming (a3's MFU 46% finding, my own #148 argument) is not sitting in the accumulation loop, so 'free throughput' is a much smaller pot than it looked; (2) peak VRAM is 67.8GB of 80GB at device batch 128, up from 34.6GB, so activations really are ~95% of memory here and nobody can stack this with a larger model or longer context - it caps the remaining search space.
